integration.description: an outside service, as data: where a person signs in to it and where its codes are exchanged, for one reached by OAuth, the hosts its credential may be sent to, and how a page shows it. A built one is installed by the host from @yaks/connections' own seed data, and marked built; any other is a custom one, owned by the space or person that made it

name.description: what a connection names it by; the entity id is derived from it, so one name is one integration

title.description: what a person calls it, written as its maker writes it: OpenRouter, Google Calendar

tagline.description: one line saying what it is, written for a person

logo.description: its mark, as an SVG document; a page draws it as an image, never as markup

authorize.description: where a person grants access, for an integration reached by OAuth

token.description: where codes and refresh tokens are exchanged; an integration with none is a pasted key

scopes.description: what a connection asks for when nothing narrower was needed

scope_separator.description: the delimiter for a provider's requested and granted OAuth scopes

pkce.description: whether the OAuth provider accepts PKCE for this client, true by default

params.description: extra parameters the authorize link carries, such as Google's access_type

auth.description: how the client authenticates at the token endpoint (default basic)

refresh_encoding.description: how the token endpoint receives refresh grants (default form)

answers.description: what the token endpoint answers: tokens (the default), or an API key, as OpenRouter's PKCE exchange does

resource.description: the resource a grant is for (RFC 8707), sent with the sign-in link and every exchange, as an MCP server asks

issuer.description: the issuer every sign-in return must name (RFC 9207), for a service that says it names one

client.description: the OAuth client it signs in as, by name: kept once as the secret `oauth_client <name>`, and shared by every integration naming it. Only a built integration signs in as a client a built one names

client_id.description: a public OAuth client's id, shipped with a built integration

name.description: the broker, by the name @yaks/connections implements it under: nango

integration.description: what the broker calls this integration: Nango's google-mail

broker.description: the broker new connections through it are made through: a service that signs a person in through its own app and hands back a fresh access token, which still goes only to `hosts`. None is direct. Changing it moves no connection: each keeps the broker it was made through

hosts.description: the API hosts a connection's credential may be sent to, and no others. None is sent nowhere: a custom key kept before anyone uses it, whose owner names its hosts once

base.description: the address its API's paths are under, on one of `hosts`: Google Calendar's https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3

docs.description: the API's reference, which says every endpoint under `base`

reads.description: read operations using a method other than GET, such as POST /query

api.description: its API, for an agent calling it as a connection: where its paths are and where they are documented. None is reached at its first host

methods.description: the only API methods a connection through it may ask for, where the service names one in each request (voip.ms's `method`): a person's own voip.ms account reads its numbers, texts, and sets where a number's texts go, and has no method that cancels or reroutes a number. None limits nothing

name.description: what an app reads it by: env.<BINDING>_<NAME> in capitals, and the field of the connection's secret it is kept as

label.description: what the connections page asks for it by, written for a person: Access key ID, API password

shown.description: typed in the open rather than masked, as a username or a region is

example.description: what it looks like, shown in the box it is typed in: an access key ID's AKIA••••••••

fields.description: what a person gives to connect a pasted-key integration, each asked for by its label: S3's access key ID, secret key and region. Kept together as the connection's secret, each with its own sentinel. None is one key; it is set when the integration is made and never changes

signature.description: how the service signs the webhooks it sends (@yaks/hook's Scheme)

testing.description: still in the service's testing mode, where only the people it lists may sign in: a page offers it only where asked to by name

built.description: installed by the host: from @yaks/connections' own seed data, or from a broker's catalog once someone connects a service it lists. Only the host writes it, so no space can mark an integration built or sign in as a built one's client

userinfo.description: OpenID endpoint naming the signed-in account when the token answer has no id_token

account.description: the field of the token endpoint's answer naming the account, as a dotted path, where it is not an email address

account_title.description: the field of the same answer naming that account for people, as a dotted path, where `account` is an id

links.description: another integration naming the person who signs in through this one, by name, whose own connection the same sign-in makes

personal.description: a person's own account at the service, such as their Discord user, which says who they are there: a connection through it belongs to whoever connects it, never to the space they connect it from

chat.description: the chat platform its connections talk through (@yaks/chat), by name: connecting it lets the Operator and the space's apps hear and answer there

chat_grant.description: the OAuth grant is the bot credential for this installation, as with a Slack workspace

instructions.description: how a person gets the credential, in markdown, written for them and for the agent helping them: where to sign up, which page issues the key, what to paste. Shown beside every connection it is needed for

example.description: what its one key looks like, shown in the box it is pasted in: ElevenLabs' sk_••••••••, Stripe's rk_live_••••••••. None shows a row of dots

mcp.description: the address of the service's own hosted MCP server, which a person connects by signing in to their account there rather than pasting a key: ElevenLabs' https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/mcp. Connecting it adds the server in the space (mcp_connect), and its tools reach the person's Operator and the apps they allow. None offers no sign-in

check.description: a call that answers 2xx once its credential works, a method and an https address on one of its hosts: GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens/verify. Its owner may change it; none checks nothing

owner.description: the space or person that made a custom integration: only its owner may change the integration's title, tagline, site or instructions, and nobody may change its hosts once they are named. A built integration has none, and is the host's

description.description: one paragraph describing the service itself and who it helps

details.description: what connecting this integration unlocks, the service data it accesses and its limitations

docs.description: the service integration documentation a person can read before connecting

connects.description: how a person connects: a pasted API key or credential fields, an OAuth sign-in, or an OAuth client of their own

categories.description: the kinds of service this catalog integration belongs to, such as crm or productivity

image.description: the address of the service logo, served through the host image door where no SVG is kept on the row

service.description: a hosted app service, whose operations are the service-marked commands in its current release declaration

app.description: the stable app identity; a rename changes no connection or order

connection.description: one link between a space or a person and an outside service, through an integration. The entity is also the secret its credential is kept as: the graph holds the handle, the vault the key or the tokens

integration.description: the integration it goes through, by name

owner.description: the space or the person it belongs to; it is deleted with them, and its credential with it

account.description: which account at the outside service, as the person would recognize it

title.description: what people call that account, where `account` is an id: a Discord server's name

scopes.description: what it was granted, or what the app that needs it asked for

status.description: needed: no credential yet; connected: one is kept; broken: the service refused it

broker.description: the broker it was made through, by name; none is made directly. It keeps working through it whatever its integration names later

via.description: the keeper, by the name the host lends it under (@yaks/host/keepers): 1password, worker

at.description: the keeper's own address for the key: a 1Password vault and item, a Worker and its secret's name

keep.description: where else its key is kept once it is given, besides the graph's own vault: each a keeper the host lends and that keeper's place for it. Each is handed the key whenever a new one is given (connection_given)

reconnecting.description: a mark on a connection a person began signing in to again at its broker, which never sends them back: whoever reads the connection settles it once the broker holds the new grant, and the mark goes. One left over an hour is dropped

anyone.description: anyone may call out through it, signed in or not, as a public widget does; otherwise only a caller holding a level on the app

each.description: each person who uses the app connects their own, and only the person who owns the connection calls out through it: set on the app's ask, the needed connection its space holds, and on the link to every person's own

binding.description: the name the app's code reads it by, env.NAME in a worker: the sentinel for its credential, or the credential itself where the link is direct

direct.description: the app's code is handed the credential itself rather than a sentinel, for a key it must transform before sending (a signature, Basic auth); only a pasted key may be

cap.description: the most calls a month that may go out through it (@yaks/egress `calls`); past it the egress refuses them until the month turns. None is no limit. Only the host sets it, never the app it caps

lends.description: on an app's link to a connection its own space keeps: the connection is lent to every copy installed from the app, which borrows it rather than asking for its own, and this is the cap each copy's link borrows it under, in calls a month. None lends it to no copy. The space owner's act, and only a sentinel every caller shares is lent: never a direct key, nor a link where each person connects their own

lender.description: on a copy's link to a connection it borrows rather than holds: the app whose lend it borrows it through. The copy's space connects a key of its own to stop borrowing, and the lender stops lending to it, either way leaving the lender's connection as it was. Only the host writes it, when the copy is installed or updated

uses.description: the relation on a link: this app calls out through that connection

asks.description: the relation on a link from a task to the connection it asks a person for: the task shows the box the key is pasted in while the connection is needed, and is completed once the key is given, kept and checked

connection_need.title: Say an app needs a connection
connection_need.description: Say that an app or a task needs an outside service: an integration by name, and the scopes it asks for. It makes a connection with no credential, owned by a space or a person, which shows them what to connect; no key or token ever passes through this tool. For a service with no built integration, name it and give the hosts its key may be sent to, and a custom integration is made for it, owned by the asking space; give it instructions too, markdown for a person and their agent saying how to get the key (where to sign up, which page issues it, what to paste), and a title, tagline and site. Its owner asking again with any of those changes them. A key kept before it is used may have no hosts yet, and is sent nowhere until its owner asks again with them; once named, its hosts never change. With each, every person who uses the app connects their own instead, and the owner connects nothing. An app that already uses a connection through that integration is answered with it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components written, followed by the integration the connection goes through, its instructions among it, to walk the person through getting the key. Asked for a task, the task shows the person the box the key is pasted in, and is completed once the key is given, kept where keep says and checked.

app.description: the app that needs it, by id or name; none when a person connects it first, or a task asks for it

owner.description: the space or person who will connect it, by id or name

scopes.description: what the app asks for; omit for the integration's own

hosts.description: for a custom key only: the hosts it may be sent to, named once, by its owner

name.description: what an app reads it by: env.<BINDING>_<NAME> in capitals, and the field of the connection's secret it is kept as

label.description: what the connections page asks for it by, written for a person: Access key ID, API password

shown.description: typed in the open rather than masked, as a username or a region is

example.description: what it looks like, shown in the box it is typed in: an access key ID's AKIA••••••••

fields.description: for a custom key only: what a person gives to connect it, when it is more than one key (an access key ID, a secret key, a region), each with a name and the label the connections page asks for it by. The app reads each as env.<BINDING>_<NAME>. Omit for one key

each.description: each person who uses the app connects their own account, rather than the owner connecting one for everyone. The host draws the Connect button for them, each person's connection shows in their own dashboard, and only they call out through it

binding.description: the name the app's code reads it by (env.NAME); omit for the integration's name in capitals

direct.description: hand the app's code the key itself rather than a sentinel, for a key it must sign with; only for a pasted key

instructions.description: for a custom integration: how a person gets its key, in markdown, written for them and the agent helping them

example.description: for a custom integration with one key: what the key looks like, shown in the box it is pasted in, its own prefix then dots: rk_live_••••••••

title.description: for a custom integration: what a person calls the service, as its maker writes it

tagline.description: for a custom integration: one line saying what the service is

site.description: for a custom integration: the service's https address on the web

task.description: the task that asks the person for the key, by id: it shows the box the key is pasted in, and is completed once the key works. The key never enters the task's text or an agent's context

via.description: the keeper, by the name the host lends it under (@yaks/host/keepers): 1password, worker

at.description: the keeper's own address for the key: a 1Password vault and item, a Worker and its secret's name

keep.description: where else the key goes once it is given, besides the graph's own vault, each a keeper the host lends (via) and its place there (at): {via: 1password, at: "Vault/Item"}, {via: worker, at: "script/SECRET_NAME"}

check.description: for a custom integration: a call that answers 2xx once the key works, a method and an https address on one of its hosts: GET https://api.example.com/v1/me

connection_list.title: List connections
connection_list.description: The connections a space or a person owns, each with its integration, account, scopes and status (needed, connected or broken), the links from each app that uses one, and the integrations they go through, with each one's instructions for getting its key. A handle is shown where a credential is kept; the credential itself never is. Returns bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and component fields.

owner.description: the space or person, by id or name

integration_install.description: install the integrations this package builds whenever a process starts working the effects; a graph already holding them as shipped is read once and written nothing

connection_given.description: once a connection's new credential is sealed in the vault: hand it to each keeper its keep names, call its integration's check, and complete each task that asks for it. A keeper that fails or a check that refuses the key leaves the run failed and the task open

integration.description: an outside service, as data: where a person signs in to it and where its codes are exchanged, for one reached by OAuth, the hosts its credential may be sent to, and how a page shows it. A built one is installed by the host from @yaks/connections' own seed data, and marked built; any other is a custom one, owned by the space or person that made it

connection.description: one link between a space or a person and an outside service, through an integration. The entity is also the secret its credential is kept as: the graph holds the handle, the vault the key or the tokens
